problems.name: Number of Islands
problems.question: Given an m x n grid of characters 1 and 0, count how many disconnected groups of land cells exist. Land cells connect vertically and horizontally.
problems.constraints: m == grid.length; n == grid[i].length; 1 <= m,n <= 300; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: All land cells are connected into one island.
There are three disconnected land components.
There is no land to count.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Each cell is pushed into the queue at most once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). DFS visits each cell once and recursion depth can reach mn.

problems.name: Clone Graph
problems.question: Given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph.
problems.constraints: 0 <= nodes <= 100; 1 <= Node.val <= 100; Node.val is unique; graph is connected from the input node.

examples.explanation: The four-node cycle is copied with new node objects.
A single isolated node is cloned.
A null input returns null.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V). BFS creates one clone per node and processes each edge once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V). DFS recursion plus the map stores cloned nodes.

problems.name: Max Area of Island
problems.question: Given a binary grid, return the maximum number of land cells in any connected island.
problems.constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 50; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: The largest four-direction component has four cells.
There is no island.
Every cell belongs to the same island.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Shared visited state avoids recounting a component.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Recursive DFS depth can include the whole grid.

problems.name: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
problems.question: Given a matrix of heights, return all cells from which water can flow to both the Pacific and Atlantic oceans.

examples.explanation: These cells can flow to both ocean borders.
The only cell touches both oceans.
Only the rightmost cell can flow to both ends in this row.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Two border BFS traversals mark all cells once per ocean.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Two DFS traversals mark all reachable cells per ocean.

problems.name: Surrounded Regions
problems.question: Given an m x n board of X and O, capture every O region fully surrounded by X by changing it to X.
problems.constraints: 1 <= m,n <= 200; board[i][j] is X or O.

examples.explanation: Only the border-connected O survives.
A single X is unchanged.
Every O touches the border.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Border BFS marks each safe cell once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Border DFS marks each safe cell once.

problems.name: Rotting Oranges
problems.question: Given a grid containing empty cells, fresh oranges, and rotten oranges, return the minimum minutes until no fresh orange remains, or -1 if impossible.
problems.constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 10; grid[i][j] is 0, 1, or 2.

examples.explanation: The infection reaches the farthest fresh orange after four minutes.
The bottom-left fresh orange is isolated.
There are no fresh oranges.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Multi-source BFS processes each orange once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Recursive layer processing consumes one BFS frontier per call.

problems.name: Walls and Gates
problems.question: Given rooms marked as walls, gates, and empty rooms, fill each empty room with its distance to the nearest gate.
problems.constraints: m == rooms.length; n == rooms[i].length; rooms use -1 for walls, 0 for gates, and 2147483647 for empty rooms.

examples.explanation: Each empty room receives the shortest gate distance.
A wall stays unchanged.
The empty room is one step from the gate.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). All gates expand together and each room is finalized once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). DFS from gates relaxes only when it improves a room distance.

problems.name: Course Schedule
problems.question: Given numCourses and prerequisite pairs, determine whether it is possible to finish every course.
problems.constraints: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; 0 <= prerequisites.length <= 5000; prerequisites[i] = [course, prerequisite].

examples.explanation: Take course 0 before course 1.
The two courses depend on each other.
There are no dependency cycles.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Kahn BFS removes zero-indegree nodes once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). DFS coloring detects back edges.

problems.name: Course Schedule II
problems.question: Given numCourses and prerequisites, return one valid order to finish all courses, or an empty array if impossible.
problems.constraints: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; 0 <= prerequisites.length <= numCourses * (numCourses - 1).

examples.explanation: Course 0 must appear before course 1.
Several valid topological orders exist.
A directed cycle prevents a valid order.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Kahn BFS processes every course and edge once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). DFS postorder builds the topological order when no cycle exists.

problems.name: Graph Valid Tree
problems.question: Given n nodes labeled 0 to n - 1 and undirected edges, return true if the edges form exactly one valid tree.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 2000; 0 <= edges.length <= 5000; edges[i] connects two distinct nodes.

examples.explanation: All nodes are connected and there is no cycle.
The edge [1,3] creates a cycle.
The graph has two components.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). BFS checks reachability after the edge count filter.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). DFS detects parent-aware cycles and connectivity.

problems.name: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
problems.question: Given n nodes and undirected edges, return the number of connected components in the graph.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 2000; 0 <= edges.length <= 5000; nodes are labeled from 0 to n - 1.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0,1,2 form one component and 3,4 form another.
All nodes are connected.
Each isolated node is its own component.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Adjacency lists let each edge be processed once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Recursive DFS visits every node and edge once.

problems.name: Redundant Connection
problems.question: Given edges of an undirected graph that started as a tree with one extra edge, return the edge that can be removed to make the graph a tree again.
problems.constraints: 3 <= edges.length <= 1000; edges[i] = [ai, bi]; nodes are labeled from 1 to edges.length.

examples.explanation: Nodes 2 and 3 are already connected through 1.
Adding [1,4] closes the cycle.
The last edge completes the triangle.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E alpha(V)); Space O(V). Union find detects the first same-component edge.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(E(V + E)); Space O(V + E). Recursive DFS checks reachability before adding each edge.

problems.name: Word Ladder
problems.question: Given beginWord, endWord, and a dictionary, return the length of the shortest transformation sequence where each step changes one character and every intermediate word is in the dictionary.
problems.constraints: 1 <= wordList.length <= 5000; all words have the same length; words contain lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: hit -> hot -> dot -> dog -> cog.
The end word is not available.
a can change directly to c.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(N * L * 26); Space O(N). BFS removes visited words once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(N * L * 26); Space O(N). Recursive BFS processes one frontier per depth.

problems.name: Open the Lock
problems.question: Given deadends and a target lock combination, return the minimum wheel turns needed to reach target from 0000, or -1 if impossible.
problems.constraints: 1 <= deadends.length <= 500; target has length 4; combinations contain digits 0 to 9.

examples.explanation: The shortest safe route takes six turns.
Turn the last wheel backward once.
The start state is blocked.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(10^4 * 8); Space O(10^4). BFS visits each combination at most once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(10^4 * 8); Space O(10^4). Recursive BFS advances one frontier layer per call.

problems.name: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
problems.question: Given an n x n binary matrix, return the length of the shortest clear path from top-left to bottom-right moving in 8 directions, or -1 if none exists.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 100; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1.

examples.explanation: Move diagonally from start to target.
The shortest path follows the right side.
The start cell is blocked.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). BFS visits each clear cell at most once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n^2). Recursive frontier expansion follows BFS layers.

problems.name: 01 Matrix

problems.constraints: 1 <= rows, cols <= 10000 total cells; mat[i][j] is 0 or 1; at least one zero exists.

examples.explanation: The center one is adjacent to a zero.
Distances grow away from the nearest zero.
Both one cells are one step from the zero.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). All zero cells expand together once.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). Recursive relaxation updates a cell only when a shorter distance is found.

problems.name: Is Graph Bipartite?

problems.constraints: 1 <= graph.length <= 100; 0 <= graph[u].length < graph.length; graph is undirected.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0,1,2 form an odd cycle conflict.
The graph can be split into {0,2} and {1,3}.
The isolated node does not affect coloring.

problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V). DFS coloring recurses through each component.
